To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a closed expression for functional determinants of general self-adjoints extensions of Laplace type operators modelled on a generalized cone.

the zeta regularizd determinant of a self-adjoint generalization of the Laplace operator on the generalized conical space-time is given by a determinant of an associated endomorphism of the space of solutions to the corresponding eigenvalue problem.

for arbitrary self-adj. ext. of a matrix of s.o.d.o. modelled on the general cone, we obtain a closed expression for \(\zeta _{\text{reg}}(s)\) and that for particular self-adj. extensions (like Friedrich’s ext.), the answer is easily obtained.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the zeta regularised determinant of Laplace type operators on the generalized cones.
the zeta function and its regularized determinant of general Laplace-type differential operators on the generalized (or conical) manifold.

the following question: Given a self-adjoint matrix of ordinary differential operators, how does the zeta regularised determinant of the matrix change when the matrix is extended to a larger matrix by adding a row and column?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the determinant of an extension of the full operator is given by a product of a finite-dimensional determinant and a one-dimensional zeta function.
the determinant of a general self-adjont extension of Laplace-type operator resulting from the generalized conic singularity can be computed from a finite-dimensional matrix.
the zeta regularised determinant of an arbitrary general self-adjont extension of a Laplace-type operator is a finite-dimensional determinant of a finite-dimensional endomorphism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a general framework for the computation of determinants of Laplace-type self-adjoint operators resulting from the zeta regularization method.
we have found a complete set of functional determinants that are relevant to the generalized cone.
the determinant of the full Laplacian is given by the determinant of the Friedrichs’ extension times a finite dimensional determinant.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of the generalized cone, the zeta regularised determinant of the Laplace-type operator can be expressed as a function of the determinant of an endormorphism of a finite dimensional vector space.
the functional determinant can be calculated in a very simple manner, once a self-adjoint boundary condition is given.
the determinant of a self-adjoint operator can be expressed in terms of a finite-dimensional endomorphism.
